title: Echo-plane replication: quota-aware traffic replication and tenant isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a production-safe traffic replication pipeline ("echo-plane") to send controlled, budgeted copies of live requests to candidate model variants for lifecycle activities (canary validation, A/B quality comparisons, offline evals). Goals: 1) enforce per-tenant cost budgets and global cost caps, 2) ensure tenant isolation and fail-safe behavior when budgets are exhausted, 3) keep online path latency unchanged (no request blocking or backpressure), and 4) expose observability and controls in the Console for rollouts/experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress-level replication that duplicates requests asynchronously to a mirror path without adding tail latency to production responses

Per-tenant and global budget enforcement: replication traffic is rate-limited by configurable daily/monthly credit buckets; when a tenant’s budget is depleted, replication is suspended for that tenant and an event is emitted
Deterministic sampling option (hash-based) and adaptive budgeted sampling controller (leaky-bucket) supporting static percent and target-cost modes
Isolation guarantees: replicated requests are routed to tenant-dedicated test pools or to namespaced model variants; access controls prevent writes to customer data stores from mirrored requests
Cost telemetry: per-tenant replication spend, token overhead, and projected burn-rate surfaced in Console with alert thresholds
Safe fallback: circuit-breaker that disables replication for impacted routes when mirror pipeline latency or error rate exceeds thresholds
E2E tests and staging run demonstrating <1ms median added p95 tail latency and cost overhead within expected tolerance for 10% sampling
work_items: Design: finalize ingress vs gateway sampling trade-offs and document decision
Infra: implement async replication queue and backpressure-safe worker pool
Controller: budgeted sampling service with per-tenant tokens and deterministic hashing option
Routing: namespaced mirror routing to dedicated test pools and tenant-scoped fallbacks
Security: ensure mirrored requests are tagged and run with reduced privileges; add audit events
Console: add replication toggle, per-tenant budget UI, and replication spend chart
Observability: metrics (replicated_requests, replication_errors, replication_latency), traces, and alert rules
E2E: staging traffic replay tests and cost burn smoke tests
Docs: runbook for disabling replication and guidance for experiment owners
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: scope to support percent-sampling + target-cost modes. Ingress sampling preferred to minimize duplicated execution paths. Design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Echo-Plane-Replication

2026-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype of sampling controller checked in (draft) - see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8213. Using a leaky-bucket per-tenant with refill window = 1h for initial experiments.

2026-02-20 - Design review: agreed on deterministic hash option for reproducible sample selection across retries (important for A/B metrics parity). Trade-off: requires stable request fingerprint; we will use tenant_id + request_id prefix hash.
2026-02-24 - QA: Integration tests added for budget exhaustion behavior. When budget hits zero, replication pipeline emits replication.suspended event and Console shows 'suspended' status.

2026-02-28 - Staging run: 24h smoke with 10% sampling on canary variant. Observed median replication enqueue latency 0.3ms, p95 added latency to production path <1ms. Cost overhead measured ~3.2% of token spend for the test config. Logs and dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/echo-plane/staging-2026-02

2026-03-01 - Security review request raised (ticket SEC-1142). Preliminary note: mirrored requests must not trigger side-effecting backend calls. Security recommended 'read-only' mirror headers and enforced namespaces. Marking security_review_required = true.

2026-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: Began working on fallback circuit-breaker. Plan: monitor worker_queue_depth and replication_error_rate; if either exceeds threshold for 30s, flip replication into 'degraded' and notify SRE. Implementation tracked in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8421
